annotation.title_clean: 無人航空機の飛行に関する許可・承認の審査要領（カテゴリーⅡ飛行）
annotation.title_en: Review Guidelines for Permission and Approval of Unmanned Aircraft Flights (Category II Flight)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT), Civil Aviation Bureau, Japan
named_instruments_referenced: Ordinance for Enforcement of the Civil Aeronautics Act
annotation.summary_en: MLIT Civil Aviation Bureau review guidelines (first issued 2015, last amended Sept 2026) for granting permission or approval for Category II drone flights under Japan's Civil Aeronautics Act. They set requirements for aircraft functions, pilot experience and skills, and safety arrangements, plus extra criteria for BVLOS, night flights, flights over events, dangerous-goods carriage, object dropping and Level 3.5 flights.
key_provisions_or_claims: Applications must be filed at least 10 business days before flight; a permit normally lasts up to 3 months, or up to 1 year for continuous operations

Aircraft must meet functional standards: no sharp protrusions, lights, the ability to stop the motor in an emergency, the ability for a person to take over autopilot, and fail-safe functions; aircraft of 25 kg or more face extra requirements
Pilots need at least 10 hours of flight experience by aircraft type, plus knowledge and skills; BVLOS flights without assistants require at least 10 hours of extra training
Level 3.5 BVLOS crossing of roads and railways using onboard cameras requires a pilot licence and third-party liability insurance
Event overflights require no-entry zones scaled to altitude and wind limits; flight logs, flight plans and accident or injury response are required
